title: TypeOpCall::getInputLocal callspec, slot, lock, size, this-pointer, and FSPEC dispatch
status_note: The locked Ghidra 12.0.4 oracle is captured twice with identical bytes. The pinned Rugra source is already a source-level MISMATCH: TypeOpCall does not override get_input_local, so the trait default returns None, and production callspec annotations use legacy AddressSpace::Iop rather than an FSPEC Varnode. Rust execution and the bilateral byte comparison intentionally remain UNTESTED in this oracle-only phase; no Cargo command was run and this evidence cannot support MATCH or L3.

decisive_semantics.references_and_outputs: Ghidra decodes the exact FuncCallSpecs pointer from input0 and returns canonical TypeFactory-owned Datatype pointers. Two FSPEC Varnodes alias the same callspec and repeated calls preserve pointer identity. Rugra's callspec object aliases correctly through Funcdata, but TypeOpCall cannot reach it and returns None.
decisive_semantics.loop_bounds_and_order: There is no container scan inside getInputLocal. The ordered guards are slot==0 or non-FSPEC, param=slot-1, parameter present, locked branch before this-pointer branch, non-void and size<=input-size, then pointer-to-struct. Fixture cases run in a fixed order and include slot 0, the final existing parameter, and the first missing parameter.
decisive_semantics.counters_and_accumulators: The only index adjustment is slot-1 exactly once after the FSPEC guard. Lock state is cleared once and restored once on the same parameter object before alias and non-FSPEC probes; no per-case callspec copies are made.
decisive_semantics.sort_and_comparison_keys: No sorting occurs. Decisive comparisons are address-space type equality with IPTR_FSPEC, parameter type-lock and this-pointer flags, metatype equality/inequality, datatype size <= input Varnode size, and canonical pointer identity in the observations. Numeric offset equality alone must not resolve the Const-space mimic.
